category: Core vocabulary: hygiene and the bathroom

examples: The cleanup took longer than the party itself.
Volunteers showed up for the river cleanup.
After the storm there were cleanups going on all over town.

entries.contrast: The noun is one word, cleanup; the verb is two, clean up.

entries.meaning: The act of washing your hands to remove germs. ---
examples: Handwashing is the simplest way to stop germs.
Signs in the restroom remind employees about handwashing.
Careful handwashing takes a full twenty seconds.

entries.meaning: A long stay in hot water, or a period of leaving something in liquid. ---
examples: She treated herself to a long soak in the tub.
Give the towel a soak in cold water.
Hot soaks help sore muscles.

entries.meaning: Grooming has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The job listing mentioned neat grooming.
Grooming takes him about ten minutes in the morning.
Personal grooming products are in aisle four.
Long-haired cats need regular grooming.
Grooming costs more than I expected.
His grooming takes about two hours.

senses.head: The care you take of your hair, nails, and general appearance
examples: The job listing mentioned neat grooming.
Grooming takes him about ten minutes in the morning.
Personal grooming products are in aisle four.

senses.head: The work of washing, brushing and trimming an animal's coat
examples: Long-haired cats need regular grooming.
Grooming costs more than I expected.
His grooming takes about two hours.

entries.русский: уход за собой, опрятность; груминг, уход за шерстью

entries.meaning: Keeping your own body clean and healthy. ---
examples: Good personal hygiene prevents a lot of illness.
The class covers personal hygiene and nutrition.
His personal hygiene had slipped while he was sick.

entries.meaning: Care of the teeth and gums by brushing and flossing. ---
examples: The dentist praised her oral hygiene.
Oral hygiene means more than just brushing.
Poor oral hygiene leads to gum disease.

entries.meaning: Thin string pulled between the teeth to clean them. ---
examples: A piece of dental floss got stuck between my teeth.
Buy the waxed dental floss.
Dental floss reaches where a brush cannot.

entries.meaning: Plaque has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Brushing removes plaque before it hardens.
The hygienist scraped the plaque off.
Plaque builds up along the gum line.
A bronze plaque marks the spot where he was born.
They gave her a plaque for thirty years of service.
Plaques along the trail explain the local history.
The scan showed plaque narrowing the artery.
These drugs can slow the buildup of plaque.
Plaque in the arteries raises the risk of a heart attack.

senses.head: The soft sticky film of bacteria that forms on teeth
examples: Brushing removes plaque before it hardens.
The hygienist scraped the plaque off.
Plaque builds up along the gum line.

senses.head: A flat piece of metal or stone fixed to a wall with writing on it
examples: A bronze plaque marks the spot where he was born.
They gave her a plaque for thirty years of service.
Plaques along the trail explain the local history.

senses.head: A fatty deposit that builds up on the inside of an artery
examples: The scan showed plaque narrowing the artery.
These drugs can slow the buildup of plaque.
Plaque in the arteries raises the risk of a heart attack.

entries.русский: зубной налёт; мемориальная доска, табличка; бляшка (в артерии)
entries.contrast: Spelled with a silent -que and pronounced PLAK.

entries.meaning: Hardened plaque that only a dentist can scrape off. ---
examples: Tartar had built up behind his front teeth.
This toothpaste claims to fight tartar.
Only a professional cleaning removes tartar.

entries.meaning: Enamel has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Soda wears away tooth enamel.
Once enamel is gone, it doesn't grow back.
The dentist said my enamel is thin.
The enamel on the old bathtub is chipped.
She collects blue enamel camping mugs.
Enamel paint holds up well on a porch railing.

senses.head: The hard white outer layer of a tooth
examples: Soda wears away tooth enamel.
Once enamel is gone, it doesn't grow back.
The dentist said my enamel is thin.

senses.head: A hard glossy coating baked onto metal or pottery
examples: The enamel on the old bathtub is chipped.
She collects blue enamel camping mugs.
Enamel paint holds up well on a porch railing.

entries.meaning: An unpleasant smell coming from someone's mouth. ---
examples: Coffee gives him bad breath.
Mouthwash only hides bad breath.
Bad breath can be a sign of gum trouble.

entries.meaning: A plastic and wire device worn to keep teeth straight after braces. ---
examples: Wear your retainer every night.
He lost his retainer in the cafeteria.
Retainers cost a few hundred dollars to replace.

entries.meaning: A removable set of false teeth. ---
examples: Grandpa soaks his dentures overnight.
Her dentures fit better after the adjustment.
He got dentures at seventy.
entries.contrast: Normally plural: a set of dentures, not a denture.

entries.meaning: Treatment that makes teeth look whiter. ---
examples: She paid for professional whitening.
Whitening can make your teeth sensitive.
The strips promise whitening in two weeks.

entries.meaning: Infection of the gums that can loosen the teeth. ---
examples: Flossing helps prevent gum disease.
Gum disease is more common than people think.
He's being treated for early gum disease.

entries.meaning: The slow breaking down of a tooth that produces cavities. ---
examples: Sugar is the main cause of tooth decay.
Fluoride slows tooth decay.
The X-ray showed tooth decay between two molars.

entries.meaning: A pain in a tooth. ---
examples: I've had a toothache since Sunday.
A bad toothache kept him up all night.
Toothaches rarely go away on their own.
entries.contrast: The -ache ending is pronounced AYK, as in cake.

entries.meaning: One of the four back teeth that come in during your late teens or twenties. ---
examples: My wisdom tooth is coming in sideways.
She had all four wisdom teeth pulled.
Not everyone gets wisdom teeth.
entries.contrast: Irregular plural: one wisdom tooth, two wisdom teeth.

entries.meaning: One of the first small teeth that a child loses around age six. ---
examples: He lost his first baby tooth today.
All her baby teeth are gone now.
A baby tooth usually falls out on its own.
entries.contrast: Americans say baby tooth; the British often say milk tooth. The plural is baby teeth.

entries.meaning: Dental treatment that cleans out the inside of a damaged tooth. ---
examples: He needs a root canal on his back molar.
The root canal took two visits.
Root canals aren't as painful as people say.

entries.meaning: A dentist who straightens crooked teeth with braces. ---
examples: The orthodontist tightened her braces.
We see the orthodontist every six weeks.
Most orthodontists start treatment around age twelve.

entries.meaning: One of the flat front teeth used for biting. ---
examples: He chipped an incisor on a fork.
Your top incisors do most of the biting.
The dentist filled a small cavity in an incisor.

entries.meaning: The unpleasant smell of stale sweat. ---
examples: Deodorant keeps body odor under control.
The gym reeked of body odor.
Nobody wants to be told they have body odor.

entries.meaning: Sweat, or the process of sweating. ---
examples: Perspiration ran down his forehead.
The shirt was soaked with perspiration.
Perspiration is how the body cools itself.
entries.contrast: Perspiration is the polite word; in ordinary speech Americans say sweat.

entries.meaning: The egg of a head louse, stuck to a hair. ---
examples: The school nurse checked the kids for nits.
Every nit has to be combed out.
Nits look like tiny white specks.

entries.meaning: A hair that curls back and grows into the skin. ---
examples: He gets ingrown hairs after shaving.
An ingrown hair can look like a pimple.
Exfoliating helps with ingrown hairs.

entries.meaning: A patch of thick hard skin, usually on a hand or foot. ---
examples: He has calluses from playing guitar.
A pumice stone smooths a callus down.
Her heels were covered in calluses.
entries.contrast: The noun is callus; callous, spelled with an o, is the adjective meaning unfeeling.

entries.meaning: The soft yellow substance that forms inside the ear. ---
examples: Earwax actually protects the ear canal.
The doctor flushed out a plug of earwax.
Cotton swabs push earwax in deeper.

entries.meaning: An itchy fungal infection of the skin between the toes.
examples: He picked up athlete's foot at the pool.
Athlete's foot spreads in damp locker rooms.
The cream cleared up his athlete's foot in a week.
